Hi Alice (and Ben/Team),

Thanks for the questions — below is a concise, technical summary you can include in your SIG/CAIQ evidence packet. I’m attaching a redacted assessment summary and our remediation log.

Assessment scope (external vendor: RedTeam Labs, test window: 2026-02-24 to 2026-03-01):
- Target: Redwood Private (customer-enclave) offering when deployed as a private control plane + customer-managed VPC for inference nodes.
- Included in scope:
  - Customer-facing ingress points (TLS termination, API gateways)
  - Network ACLs and SGs attached to inference nodes in customer VPC (data plane boundaries)
  - Inter-node RPC and KV cache endpoints where they cross tenant/network boundaries
  - Service control plane endpoints hosted in Redwood-managed VPC where relevant for auth/token exchange
- Excluded from scope:
  - Third-party SaaS used by customer for unrelated services
  - Internal dev/test environment (not representative of private deployment)

Boundary assumptions — what we relied on for the assessment:
- Customer-managed VPC was treated as the primary data plane; Redwood’s responsibility (for the test) was to validate controls where Redwood-managed network paths interface with that VPC (e.g., peering/transit gateways, NATs).
- The assessment assumed standard VPC route tables and that customers apply the recommended security group baseline in our deployment guide (we supplied the baseline config).
- KV cache encryption-in-transit and TLS mutual auth were tested only for inter-service links that cross the boundary; ephemeral keys for KV cache were out of scope for the vendor (handled by our internal review).

Findings & remediation status (summary):
- Finding 1: Weak host-level hardening on a small subset of inference nodes in the customer-enclave testbed (CVSS 6.2). Remediation: host images rebuilt with CIS baseline, patch applied. Status: verified by Redwood (internal) 2026-03-05; vendor re-test scheduled.
- Finding 2: Misconfigured security group allowing overly permissive SSH from a management CIDR used during initial setup. Remediation: SG tightened to management subnet + jump host model. Status: vendor verified 2026-03-10 (see RTC-Report-2026-03-01.pdf excerpt).
- Finding 3: Ambiguous assumption in report about whether KV cache endpoints are dual-homed across control/data networks. Remediation: clarified architecture diagram, added explicit ACLs and mTLS. Status: mitigation implemented 2026-03-14; verification pending vendor re-test.

Deliverables attached/shared:
- Redwood_External_Assessment_Summary.pdf (redacted vendor executive summary)
- RTC-Report-2026-03-01.pdf (vendor full technical report — redacted, limited distribution)
- MVP-Remediation-Log.csv (detailed fix dates, owners, JIRA links)

Next steps we propose for FirstContact:
1) We will provide a one-page redacted summary you can attach to SIG/CAIQ. (attached)
2) Vendor re-test is scheduled for week of 2026-03-22 — we will share the pass/fail and any follow-up findings.
3) If you want, we can run a scoped attestation that explicitly covers the KV cache boundary case once the vendor issues results.

If you need any additional wording for CAIQ control responses (for example how we isolate control plane from data plane in private deployments), let me know and I’ll draft a short paragraph for your packet.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Security | Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com

Hi Alice — quick follow-up with the specifics you asked for and verification items after the vendor re-test:

KV cache network posture:
- Cache hosts are single-interface within the customer VPC (data plane). There is no dual-homing of cache instances into Redwood-managed control networks.
- Cross-network traffic is proxied through a dedicated gateway (deployed in the customer VPC) that performs TLS termination and enforces mTLS to Redwood control plane endpoints. We added explicit ACLs on that gateway and removed any direct routing between cache hosts and control-plane subnets.

Vendor re-test result (RedTeam Labs):
- Re-test completed 2026-03-22. Outcome: pass for previously verified items (Finding 2). Finding 1: confirmed fixed; vendor marked as closed. Finding 3: mitigation implemented; vendor requested targeted verification for KV-mTLS configuration — vendor completed verification of mTLS and ACLs with a small set of active tests and marked the issue as "verified with recommendation" (no active exploit found). Full vendor report excerpt is attached (redacted).

Remediation timeline & access notes:
- All fixes implemented by 2026-03-14. Vendor re-test completed 2026-03-22.
- Evidence bundle: redacted vendor excerpt + remediation log uploaded to the shared Drive folder. Permission: FirstContact security group granted view access to folder link below; if you need download access please reply and I’ll add individuals.
